summary: This defines a RobotPet class: a blueprint that stores a pet's name, battery level, and mood, and can report the trick it performs. It is the code under test in this chapter's first unit test.

lines.text: Declares the class, the template from which individual robot pets are created. A class on its own runs nothing; it waits until something creates an object from it.
The initializer runs automatically whenever a new RobotPet is created, and it receives the three starting values for that pet.
Stores the name on the object itself so that each pet remembers its own name after the initializer finishes.
Keeps the battery level as part of the object's state, which is exactly the kind of value a unit test can check with assertEqual.
Records the pet's mood, completing the three attributes that describe one robot pet.
Defines a behaviour that every robot pet shares. Because it returns a value instead of printing one, a test can capture the result and compare it.
Returns the default talent for a plain RobotPet, the baseline that subclasses will later override. The f prefix does nothing useful here since there are no placeholders in the braces.
